title: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura — The Seventh Goswami
description: Appearance day celebration quiz on the life, divine pastimes, and preaching legacy of Śrīla Saccidānanda Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura from 'The Seventh Goswami'.

questions.question: What birth name was given to Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura at his birth in Birnagar in 1838?
questions.explanation: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura was born on September 2, 1838, in Birnagar (Ulāgrām) and was named Kedāranātha Datta by his father, Ānanda-chandra Datta.

questions.question: Which of the following masterworks were composed or compiled by Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Jaiva-dharma, Śaraṇāgati, and Gītāvalī were authored by Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura. Caitanya-caritāmṛta was written by Śrīla Kṛṣṇadāsa Kavirāja Gosvāmī in the 16th century.

questions.question: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura strictly managed his daily schedule as a government magistrate, sleeping from 8 PM to midnight and writing his devotional literatures during the quiet late-night hours.
questions.explanation: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura maintained an extraordinary daily schedule, retiring at 8 PM, rising at midnight to write until 4 AM, and fulfilling his judicial duties punctually during the day.

questions.context: Spoken in intense spiritual ecstasy upon being brought in a basket to the mound discovered by Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura at Ballāldīghi (Māyāpur).
questions.explanation: The venerable Śrīla Jagannātha dāsa Bābājī Mahārāja, who was over 120 years old, leaped out of his carrying basket and danced in ecstasy at the site, confirming the authentic birthsite of Lord Caitanya.

questions.assertion: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura prayed intensely to the Supreme Lord to send a 'ray of Viṣṇu' to assist him in spreading pure Kṛṣṇa consciousness.
questions.reason: He recognized that the widespread degradation of Lord Caitanya's teachings by deviant sahajiyā sects required an empowered soul to re-establish pure Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇavism.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true, and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.
Both Assertion and Reason are true, but Reason is NOT the correct explanation of Assertion.
Assertion is true, but Reason is false.
Assertion is false, but Reason is true.
questions.explanation: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura prayed for a divine successor because the true teachings of Lord Caitanya were obscured by deviant sects, leading to the birth of his son Bimala Prasāda (Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura).

questions.passage: In 1894, after retiring from government service, Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura went door-to-door in Calcutta begging five hundred rupees from each wealthy landlord to construct the temple at Yoga-pīṭha. His humble begging campaign was highlighted in the Amrita Bazar Patrika.
options: He begged one rupee (not five hundred rupees) from each Hindu gentleman.
He collected funds in Navadvīpa rather than Calcutta.
The newspaper report appeared in the Times of India rather than Amrita Bazar Patrika.
questions.explanation: As reported in the Amrita Bazar Patrika on December 6, 1894, Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura humbly went door-to-door in Calcutta begging just one rupee from each Hindu gentleman for the Gaur Vishnupriya Temple Fund.
questions.reference: Chapter 21: Retirement and Expansion of Preaching

questions.question: Identify the item that does NOT belong with the others among Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura's writings and service:
When Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura established the Nāma-haṭṭa ('Marketplace of the Holy Name') and traveled extensively through Bengal chanting and lecturing, what was the immediate result?
options: Over 500 Nāma-haṭṭa centers were established, inspiring thousands of ordinary citizens and villagers to take up Harināma-saṅkīrtana.
The British government immediately revoked his pension and forced him to return to judicial service.
He was banned from entering the district of Nadia by local caste scholars.
He stopped writing devotional books to focus exclusively on agriculture.
questions.explanation: Through his structured Nāma-haṭṭa preaching, Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura established more than 500 congregational preaching centers (saṅgas) across Bengal, creating a massive spiritual revival.

options: In his Nāma-haṭṭa preachings, Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura humbly described himself as the 'sweeper' of the marketplace of the Holy Name.
Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura published the English booklet 'Shree Chaitanya Mahaprabhu - His Life and Precepts' and sent copies to Western universities including McGill University in Canada.
Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura retired from government service at the young age of thirty to live as a reclusive hermit in Vrindavan.
questions.explanation: Statement 3 is FALSE. Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura retired from government service in 1894 at the age of 56 (not thirty) after decades of active service as a magistrate, and he engaged in dynamic preaching rather than reclusive retirement.

questions.scenario: While serving as magistrate in Chāmparāṇ, Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura noticed that local residents were terrified of an evil spirit (brahma-daitya) living in a Banyan tree that influenced mindsets and court decisions. To free the people from fear without resorting to mundane force, he took a spiritual course of action.
questions.question: What decisive spiritual action did Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura take to deliver the place from the ghost?
options: He engaged a learned paṇḍita to recite the Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam under the tree for one month, after which the tree fell and the ghost departed.
He ordered the British army to cut down the Banyan tree with axes.
He performed a fire sacrifice with fifty tantric priests to exorcise the spirit.
He relocated the entire township three miles away to escape the tree's influence.
questions.explanation: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura engaged a paṇḍita to recite Śrīmad-Bhāgavatam beneath the Banyan tree. Upon completion of the one-month recitation, the tree collapsed and the brahma-daitya was liberated.

questions.scenario: When the editor and founder of the Amrita Bazar Patrika, Śiśir Kumār Ghosh, met Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura and observed his saintly scholarly life, he remarked: 'I have not seen the Six Gosvāmīs of Vrindavan, but I consider you to be the Seventh Goswāmī.' How does a genuine Vaiṣṇava practitioner view such praise?
questions.question: In accord with Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura's teachings in Śaraṇāgati and Sva-niyama-dvādaśakam, how should a devotee respond to personal honor?
options: Remain deeply humble, attribute all credit to the spiritual master and Lord Gaurāṅga, and avoid taking pride in personal praise.
Demand financial compensation and titles from religious assemblies.
Publicly boast about one's achievements to gain political influence.
Reject all devotional service and cease writing books.
questions.explanation: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura exemplified perfect humility (amāninā mānadena), viewing all accomplishments as the mercy of Śrī Caitanya Mahāprabhu and his guru line.

questions.question: Which journal, founded by Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura in 1881, served as the premier monthly Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava magazine for educating educated society in Bengal?
questions.explanation: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura started the monthly magazine Sajjana-toṣaṇī in 1881, which was later published in English as The Harmonist by Śrīla Bhaktisiddhānta Sarasvatī Ṭhākura.

questions.question: Which of the following key places in the Nadia/Navadvīpa region are intimately associated with Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura's life and preaching? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Svānanda-sukhada-kuñja, Yoga-pīṭha (Lord Caitanya's birthplace), and Surabhi-kuñja are all located in the sacred Navadvīpa-dhāma region where Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura performed his bhajana and preaching.

questions.question: On what date was Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura born in Birnagar (West Bengal)?
questions.explanation: Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura was born on Sunday, September 2, 1838, in the ancient village of Birnagar (Ulāgrām) in the Nadia district.

questions.question: Which of the following prominent spiritual songbooks were composed by Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura to express the moods of surrender and devotion? (Select all that apply)
questions.explanation: Śaraṇāgati, Kalyāṇa-kalpataru, and Gītāvalī are songbooks composed by Śrīla Bhaktivinoda Ṭhākura. Gīta-govinda was written in the 12th century by Jayadeva Gosvāmī.

questions.question: What title was awarded to Kedāranātha Datta by the Vaiṣṇava scholars (Ācārya Kula) in 1886 in recognition of his extraordinary devotional writings and preaching?
questions.explanation: In 1886, the Gauḍīya Vaiṣṇava scholars formally awarded Kedāranātha Datta the title 'Bhaktivinoda' ('one who pleases the Lord through devotional service').
